# Mechanica

> A Scrap Mechanic-style physics sandbox (Godot 4 .NET, Jolt physics, Lua part scripts, host-authoritative
> multiplayer). An AI can play and mod it through a JSON-RPC 2.0 WebSocket endpoint on the host
> (`--host --ai`): every game action is a method, `mechanica.describe` returns JSON Schemas for all of
> them, and `mechanica.join` gives the AI a player of its own.

## For an AI

- [System prompt](docs/ai/system-prompt.md): what the game is and how to behave, ready to use
- [Method reference](docs/ai/reference.md): every method with its params, generated from the game
- [Method schemas](docs/ai/describe.json): the same as JSON Schemas, for tool lists
- [Playing guide](docs/ai/playing.md): joining, seeing, moving, building, surviving, quests
- [Modding guide](docs/ai/modding.md): reading and changing mods, packages
- [Bug-hunting guide](docs/ai/bug-hunting.md): exploring, reproducing and reporting

## For people connecting an AI

- [Overview](docs/ai/README.md)
- [AI endpoint](docs/ai-endpoint.md): starting it, tokens and scopes, protocol, events

## Optional
